title: ICICI Bank Profit Jumps 20% to Rs 14,843 Crore in Second Quarter
excerpt: Net interest income rose 17.7% to Rs 25,339 crore, gross NPA fell to 1.20% and loans grew 30%, as India's second-largest private lender beat profit estimates.
body:
• ICICI Bank's standalone net profit rose 20.1% year on year to Rs 14,843 crore in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, beating the Rs 14,251 crore analysts expected, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters.
  • Net interest income rose 17.7% to Rs 25,339 crore, while net interest margin narrowed to 4.18% from 4.36% in the June quarter.
  • Asset quality improved: gross NPA fell to 1.20% from 1.38% a quarter earlier, net NPA to 0.30%, and provisions fell 6.9% to Rs 851 crore.
  • For investors: loans grew 30% and deposits 27.1% year on year, fee income rose 20.1%, and capital adequacy stood at 16.68% with CET-1 at 16.01%.

ICICI Bank reported a standalone net profit of Rs 14,843 crore for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 20.1% from Rs 12,359 crore a year earlier, driven by strong loan growth and lower provisions. The result beat expectations: analysts had forecast Rs 14,251 crore, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters. Consolidated net profit rose 22.3% to Rs 16,333 crore.

The board approved the results at a meeting in Mumbai on October 17, 2026, the bank said in its regulatory filing, reported by The Economic Times. The statutory auditors issued an unmodified limited review report.

Core Income and Margins

Net interest income, the difference between interest earned and interest paid, rose 17.7% year on year to Rs 25,339 crore, from Rs 21,529 crore in the same quarter last year. Net interest margin narrowed to 4.18%, from 4.30% a year earlier and 4.36% in the June quarter — the one soft line in an otherwise strong set of numbers, and a sign that deposit costs are still pressuring lending spreads across Indian banking.

Core operating profit grew 21.8% to Rs 20,805 crore. Excluding dividend income from subsidiaries, it rose 25.0% to Rs 20,342 crore. Fee income grew 20.1% to Rs 7,795 crore, with retail, rural and business banking customers accounting for about 75% of fees. Non-interest income excluding treasury rose 12.5% to Rs 8,277 crore, while the treasury desk recorded a loss of Rs 230 crore against a gain of Rs 220 crore a year earlier. Operating expenses rose a controlled 8.5% to Rs 12,811 crore, well below revenue growth.

Loans, Deposits and the Balance Sheet

Total advances rose 30.0% year on year to Rs 18,31,580 crore at September 30, 2026. Excluding loans from international branches against FCNR (B) deposits, underlying loan growth was 24.1%. Retail and rural loans grew 14.8% and made up 51.6% of the book. Business banking expanded 33.8% and the domestic corporate portfolio 30.6%.

Period-end deposits rose 27.1% year on year to Rs 20,49,874 crore, though excluding FCNR (B) deposits the underlying growth was 17.0%. Average deposits rose 21.2% to Rs 18,88,219 crore, and the average CASA ratio stood at 35.8%. The bank added 145 branches in the first half, taking its network to 7,656 branches and 12,143 ATMs and cash recycling machines.

Asset Quality and Capital

The gross non-performing asset ratio improved to 1.20% at September 30, from 1.38% at June 30 and 1.58% a year earlier. The net NPA ratio fell to 0.30%, from 0.35% a quarter earlier and 0.39% a year earlier. Gross NPA additions were Rs 4,833 crore, down from Rs 5,034 crore a year earlier. Provisions fell to Rs 851 crore, from Rs 1,260 crore in the June quarter and Rs 914 crore a year earlier.

The bank held contingency provisions of Rs 13,100 crore, plus an additional standard asset provision of Rs 1,283 crore for its agricultural priority sector portfolio, made as directed by the Reserve Bank of India. Capital adequacy stood at 16.68% and the CET-1 ratio at 16.01%, comfortably above the regulatory minimums of 11.70% and 8.20% cited in its results.

Subsidiaries and What Comes Next

Among subsidiaries, ICICI Lombard General Insurance reported profit of Rs 946 crore, ICICI Prudential AMC Rs 889 crore, ICICI Securities Rs 439 crore, ICICI Prudential Life Rs 374 crore for the quarter, and ICICI Home Finance Rs 220 crore. Consolidated assets grew 22.6% to Rs 32,92,953 crore. The bank also said it had applied to the RBI for an extension of Pradeep Kumar Sinha's tenure as non-executive part-time chairperson, from July 1, 2027 to February 16, 2029.

For investors, the quarter supports the case that India's second-largest private lender by market capitalisation can grow its loan book at 30% while still improving asset quality. The watchpoints are the margin — down 18 basis points in a quarter — and whether deposit growth excluding the FCNR (B) inflow can keep pace with credit demand.
